Customer to open support ticket for VPC peering issue by 12/11
Schedule canary run for inference traffic (10% load) w/c 12/15
Security to review SOC2 artifact link sent by Redwood prior to 12/14
action_items: Alex Chen: send benchmark spreadsheet + quantization profiles (due 2026-12-12)
Sofia Martinez: confirm IAM role & VPC CIDR to enable peering (due 2026-12-11)
Priya Rao: produce short runbook for KV cache warmup for their dataset (due 2026-12-13)

summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access & VPC peering issues, initial tuning results for latency/cost tradeoffs. Redwood AE + SE reviewed recent benchmark runs, recommended quantization and batching tweaks. Customer to resolve VPC peering and IAM role so Dedicated test cluster can run. Next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, schedule canary week of 12/15, security follow-up on KMS and SOC2 artifacts.
transcript:
00:00 - Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on for 45 minutes, is that still good?
00:05 - Daniel Park: yeah, that works for us, thanks Alex.
00:10 - Alex Chen: quick roll call? we'll have Priya from eng to run through the tuning numbers.
00:15 - Priya Rao: hey all, Priya here.
00:18 - Sofia Martinez: Sofia here.
00:20 - Michael Lee: Michael, security.
00:22 - Tara O'Neill: Tara, product.
00:24 - Jamal Khan: Jamal, ops.
00:27 - Alex Chen: great, agenda — onboarding updates, review the benchmark spreadsheet from last night's run, discuss VPC peering/IAM issues blocking Dedicated cluster, and plan the canary.
01:05 - Daniel Park: good. quick context, our goal is to validate latency under 120ms p95 for short clinical prompts and keep cost per 1k tokens under our internal threshold — aiming for a 30% improvement vs current API spend.
01:30 - Alex Chen: perfect, that's aligned. Priya, can you recap the runs? I saw results in the shared sheet but want to highlight.
01:45 - Priya Rao: sure, so we ran three profiles overnight: hosted baseline using rwd-model-v1 (fp16), then a 4-bit quantized variant, and a batching config with max_batch 8 and async batching. The baseline p95 averaged ~150ms on their 256-token workloads, quantized went to ~120-130ms, batching helped throughput but spiked tail a bit when load was uneven.
02:20 - Jamal Khan: when you say quantized, that's int4? we need to be precise because our infra team will worry about numeric drift for clinical text.
02:30 - Priya Rao: yes, it's 4-bit QAT-style quant in the Redwood pipeline, we did QA on a held-out prompt set — top-line semantic similarity stayed >0.98 for our eval metrics but we can share the examples.
03:00 - Tara O'Neill: was there any generation quality regressions that product should be worried about? like hallucinations or missing steps in multi-turn?
03:12 - Priya Rao: small increase in conservative answers for very long context but for the 3-6 sentence clinical notes it's fine. We flagged two prompts where tokenization differences changed punctuation, but not meaning.
03:45 - Daniel Park: ok good. next item — access. Sofia?
03:50 - Sofia Martinez: so VPC peering attempt yesterday failed — looks like the IAM role we provided didn't have ec2:CreateVpcPeeringConnection permission and their infra blocks cross-account peering by default. Our network team needs you to confirm exact CIDR ranges.
04:10 - Alex Chen: understood — we requested the CIDR in the onboarding form, can you paste it in the chat?
04:20 - Sofia Martinez: will do after. also the temporary bastion we set up for the SE to push the config timed out; maybe session manager or SSM isn't configured on your side.
04:35 - Priya Rao: that explains why some of our remote probes failed. Jamal, do you have an update on enabling SSM?
04:45 - Jamal Khan: SSM is not enabled for that subnet yet, security flagged it, we'll need a short exception or we can do a jump box with stricter rules.
05:00 - Michael Lee: from security side, we prefer SSM since it gives session audit logs. We'll share the SSM setup checklist.
05:12 - Alex Chen: great — Michael, we'll send the SOC2 artifact link and KMS integration doc for review. Any initial red flags?
05:25 - Michael Lee: KMS integration looks straightforward but need to confirm key rotation policies and whether Redwood supports HSM-backed keys. Also we want separation of logs — application logs vs customer data — ensure those aren't mixed.
05:45 - Alex Chen: yes we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) and can work with HSM options for Private deployments; we'll include our KMS doc and an example CloudTrail query to show log partitioning.
06:10 - Priya Rao: back to tuning — we also tried prefix caching (KV warmup) for repeated clinical templates; that dropped latency by ~15ms for cached prefixes but only helps when traffic has repetition. We have a runbook for cache warmup steps.
06:40 - Daniel Park: that could be big since a lot of our calls reuse templates. Can you share warmup sequence?
06:50 - Priya Rao: yes, action item for me to share runbook.
07:00 - Alex Chen: ok, now the benchmark specifics — I'll call out numbers from the sheet: baseline cost per 1k tokens was $2.10, quantized dropped to $1.45, batching optimized to $1.20 but p95 tail moved from 120ms to 170ms in one of the spikes.
07:25 - Tara O'Neill: spike concerns product because user facing latency variability is worse than steady slightly higher latency.
07:35 - Priya Rao: right, for user-facing paths we recommend combining small batch size (4) + prefix caching + async immediate flush for low-latency flows; reserve larger batches for background summarization.
07:55 - Alex Chen: suggestion: run two routes — low-latency route pinned to hosted cpu-optimized nodes with small batch / no quantization, and background route to quantized dedicated for bulk jobs. That matches Redwood Optimize patterns.
08:15 - Daniel Park: makes sense — we have separate endpoints for real-time assistant vs nightly ingestion, so we can route. What's the effort to set that up?
08:25 - Priya Rao: we can spin up dedicated pool for the background route in a day once VPC peering and IAM are set. Hosted adjustments for low-latency are config only — we can update your API routes.
08:40 - Alex Chen: timeline check — if network is unblocked by 12/11 and we get IAM sorted, we can do a canary 10% traffic run next week (w/c 12/15). Priya, can you run the canary config?
08:55 - Priya Rao: yes, I'll prepare canary config and share the exact traffic split.
09:05 - Sofia Martinez: one more network note — our security team requires explicit IP allowlist and an expiration for temporary peering. Can Redwood support ephemeral peering or do we need permanent setup?
09:20 - Alex Chen: ephemeral peering is supported for Private deployments via scheduled peering tokens in our infra. For Dedicated we typically do a long-lived peering; but we can do time-limited tunnels for the canary. We'll send options.
09:40 - Michael Lee: also need to see session-level audit logs for the canary run. We want to validate no PII leakage in debug logs.
09:50 - Priya Rao: yes logs are scrubbed by default but we'll include explicit config to mask PII and show the logging separation.
10:05 - Daniel Park: on the evaluation side, can Redwood deliver the example prompts that regressed post-quantization and the similarity scores so we can check with our clinical reviewers?
10:18 - Priya Rao: absolutely, I'll attach the two flagged prompts and the eval scores in the spreadsheet.
10:28 - Tara O'Neill: what about model rollbacks if quality dips during canary?
10:33 - Alex Chen: we have automatic fallback policies — canary can be configured to roll back to the hosted baseline if semantic similarity drops below a threshold or if p95 exceeds SLO by X. We'll include recommended thresholds.
11:00 - Jamal Khan: surprised there's no mention of certificate exchange — do we need mutual TLS for the Dedicated pool?
11:10 - Alex Chen: mutual TLS is optional; we can enable mTLS and provide cert bundles for the Dedicated cluster. We'll include cert rotation guidance.
11:25 - Michael Lee: please also include any SLA language for the Dedicated canary — even provisional.
11:35 - Alex Chen: we'll share a short canary SLA note.
11:45 - Daniel Park: sounds good. items recap?
11:50 - Alex Chen: recap: Redwood sends updated benchmark spreadsheet + tuning notes (Alex), Priya sends KV cache warmup runbook and flagged prompts, Redwood sends SOC2/KMS artifacts link (Alex), customer to confirm CIDR and enable SSM / IAM role (Sofia/Jamal), schedule canary for week of 12/15 once peering done.
12:20 - Tara O'Neill: can we get the benchmark spreadsheet by Friday?
12:25 - Alex Chen: yes, we'll send by 12/12 EOD.
12:30 - Michael Lee: I'll review KMS docs by 12/14.
12:35 - Daniel Park: thanks everyone.
12:40 - Alex Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in email and update the ticket tracker. bye.
12:45 - meeting ended
